title: Accendi il tuo primo LED

manualEvidence.evidence: LED, breadboard, 9V battery with clip, and 470 Ohm resistor (Viola Giallo Marrone) are required; the book lists no extra jumper wires.

Battery positive goes to the red breadboard strip; the 470 Ohm resistor links that strip to a free hole in the zone below; the LED straddles the central divide with the long leg facing the resistor and the short leg beyond the divide.
Battery negative goes straight to a free hole in the same tie as the LED short leg, closing the circuit and turning the LED on; the figures show only the two battery-clip leads.

driftNotes: Component and wire data match experiments-vol1.js and the lesson-path build_circuit intent.

Book-faithful topology (pages 29-31): LED straddles the central divide (anode f3 top block, cathode e3 bottom block, shared tie 3 with the resistor), no green channel bridge, battery negative returns directly to tie 3 without any bus-minus chain.

Declared residual delta: the book plugs one resistor leg straight into the red strip; the circuit data grammar only places component pins in board holes, so one red jumper (bus-top-plus-9 to j9) stands in for that leg. Wire total is 3 here versus 2 leads in the book figures.

The book leaves hole positions free ('punto qualsiasi'); tie 9 (resistor rail side) and tie 3 (LED) are the canonical choices recorded here. Taken literally, the page 30-31 drawings place LED, resistor and negative lead on three different ties, which would leave the circuit open; the page text (long leg toward the resistor, negative on the short-leg column) is the binding source.
The lesson-path book_reference points to page 29 only; this fixture records manual evidence across pages 29-31.
